discovered.name: Remember November 2026 / Polar Bear 2026
discovered.whyConsidered: A 2023 AI polar-bear 'meme from the future' revived in late Aug-Sept 2026 with the line 'Remember November 2026 is coming'. It has a built-in calendar payoff (Nov 2026), KYM entries plus a Yahoo-syndicated explainer, and independent sellers already listing merch.

discovered.name: Kinda Chic trend ('kinda chic to...')
discovered.whyConsidered: A phrase template with high identity value: people reframe ordinary wins as 'chic'. Celebrities and brands adopted it, it got press in multiple countries and languages, and Etsy sellers are already making niche variants.

discovered.name: Jimothy the raccoon (Seattle)
discovered.whyConsidered: The clearest merch-demand story in the lens: Fast Company/Shopifreaks reported a merch flood, there is an officially licensed bobblehead, Mariners tie-ins, and a reported $20K+ card resale. It went viral in July but kept accelerating Aug-Oct through brand tie-ins (Fortnite sidekick on Oct 1).

discovered.name: Things to Say (ironic hustle-culture advice lists)
discovered.rejectReason: The format depends on celebrity photos (e.g., Matthew McConaughey), which can't be used on merch. The first post was sexual. No merch or purchase signals found. A photo-free 'list of terrible advice' card is possible but generic and loses the joke.
discovered.whyConsidered: Won KYM's September 2026 Meme of the Month with 11.6% of votes (per KYM poll result in search). Started on TikTok Aug 17, 2026.

discovered.name: Chile memes (everything in Chile is long and skinny)
discovered.rejectReason: A spectator joke with no merch, shop or purchase signals in search results. The product angle (skinny-object stickers) is weak, and jokes about a real country risk reading as mockery to buyers.
discovered.whyConsidered: Came 2nd in KYM's September 2026 Meme of the Month (8.4%). Wide TikTok/Reels/X spread in September.

discovered.name: Thoughts on Lanterns (edit format)
discovered.rejectReason: Built on a promo still from DC/HBO's 'Lanterns' and the actors' likenesses (Aaron Pierre, Kyle Chandler). Edits pile third-party IP on top. Not usable on merch.
discovered.whyConsidered: Big X/Twitter exploitable in September 2026 (53K+ likes on the Sept 8 post, per KYM summary).

discovered.name: La Peace (Kai Cenat 'lapis lazuli' clip)
discovered.rejectReason: Built around a streamer's likeness and persona plus Minecraft. Without Kai Cenat the phrase means nothing to buyers. Right-of-publicity risk.
discovered.whyConsidered: 2nd in KYM's August 2026 Meme of the Month (~11%). The Aug 16 TikTok edit got 4.2M views in five days (per KYM summary).

discovered.name: Quiet on the Creek
discovered.rejectReason: The phrase is the title and hook of a Saucy Santana song released Jul 17, 2026, and the artist actively markets it (The Fader interview, Aug 24). Merch would trade on an artist's lyric/title. Pass on rights.
discovered.whyConsidered: The strongest slang spread in the lens. #QuietontheCreek was reported No. 1 on TikTok music, the song debuted at No. 45 on Billboard Hot R&B/Hip-Hop (per KYM/meme.com summaries), and it's used as 'move in silence' slang.

discovered.name: Grr Mondays
discovered.rejectReason: The source image is a crude Universal film scene and can't be used. The bare phrase lands in the saturated 'I hate Mondays' office-mug category. No merch signal found.
discovered.whyConsidered: A Ted 2 (2015) line resurfaced on TikTok in Sept 2026 as Monday-complaint shorthand. Short and mug-friendly.

discovered.name: Relax, Pal
discovered.rejectReason: It comes from news coverage of a hazing investigation (arrests Sept 25, 2026). Memes glorify a private student tied to a criminal case. Ethical and right-of-publicity concerns; do not monetize.
discovered.whyConsidered: A late-September 2026 catchphrase from a WISN 12 news clip that spread fast on TikTok.

discovered.name: We can't all be matcha girls (hot-dog boys, M&M girls, pretzel people)
discovered.rejectReason: Only one source (Epidemic Sound roundup), so not enough evidence of spread. 'M&M' is a Mars trademark.
discovered.whyConsidered: Identity-style food-coded phrase listed in a September 2026 TikTok trend roundup.

discovered.name: You were bought ('I just spent $1 for one view')
discovered.rejectReason: An audio-driven clickbait format set to a commercial song (Clean Bandit & Zara Larsson). No product angle.
discovered.whyConsidered: Reported as trending for over a month in Sept 2026 (Epidemic Sound roundup).

discovered.name: 6-7 New Year angle ('the next 2 years are literally 6-7')
discovered.rejectReason: Older than this lens's window (6-7 was Dictionary.com's 2025 Word of the Year), and Etsy, Amazon and Redbubble already list '2026 2027 literally 6-7' tees and PNGs, so it's saturated. Trademark status unverified. Flag for the seasonal/New Year agent rather than this lens.
discovered.whyConsidered: 2026->2027 reads as '6 7'. 6-7 is still the most-searched Gen Alpha slang of 2026 (Euronews, Sept 28, 2026). New Year's Eve is a natural trigger.

discovered.name: Elizabeth Holmes / Nathan Fielder documentary memes
discovered.rejectReason: Real-person likeness. Spectator meme with no product angle.
discovered.whyConsidered: Named in KYM's September 2026 Meme of the Month roundup.

discovered.name: Let's Groove edits
discovered.rejectReason: Animation edits set to an Earth, Wind & Fire song. Song rights; nothing to put on a product.
discovered.whyConsidered: 3rd in KYM's September 2026 Meme of the Month (7.4%).

discovered.name: Lesbian Space Princess 'Great Fandom Truce'
discovered.rejectReason: A pile-on mocking a film: criticism, not demand. Film IP, and it would target a real production.
discovered.whyConsidered: Won KYM's August 2026 Meme of the Month (13.3%).

discovered.name: Gen Alpha back-to-school slang (larp/larper, bop, chud, geeg)
discovered.rejectReason: The search interest comes from confused parents looking up meanings, not purchase intent. 'Bop' has a sexual meaning and 'chud' is a slur-like insult. 'Geeg' had no definition in results.
discovered.whyConsidered: Explainer coverage of the most-searched slang (Euronews Sept 28, 2026; Mental Floss; Yahoo).

discovered.name: Petra Parker / Gucci Morty / Universal Horror Nights roaming-character memes
discovered.rejectReason: Built on Marvel, Adult Swim (Rick and Morty) and Universal IP.
discovered.whyConsidered: August 2026 Meme of the Month contenders.

discovered.name: Malfoid (female Draco Malfoy fan art)
discovered.whyConsidered: Blew up on X in late September 2026 (per Yahoo/KYM-sourced search summary).
